translation_en: Hannad ibn al-Sari narrated to us: Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar: Simak al-Hanafi narrated to me: I heard Ibn 'Abbas say: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab related to me. He said: On the day of Badr... Another chain: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—the wording is his—'Umar ibn Yunus al-Hanafi narrated to us: 'Ikrimah ibn 'Ammar narrated to us: Abu Zumayl, Simak al-Hanafi, narrated to me: 'Abdullah ibn 'Abbas narrated to me: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: On the day of Badr, the Messenger of Allah looked at the polytheists, who numbered one thousand, while his Companions numbered three hundred and nineteen men. The Prophet of Allah faced the direction of prayer, then stretched out his hands and called out to his Lord: O Allah, fulfill for me what You promised me. O Allah, grant me what You promised me. O Allah, if this group of Muslims is destroyed, You will not be worshipped on earth. He continued calling out to his Lord, stretching out his hands and facing the direction of prayer, until his cloak fell from his shoulders. Abu Bakr came, picked up the cloak, placed it back on his shoulders, and embraced him from behind. He said: Prophet of Allah, this earnest appeal to your Lord is enough; He will surely fulfill what He promised you. Then Allah, Mighty and Exalted, revealed: When you sought your Lord's help, He answered you: I will reinforce you with a thousand angels, one after another (8:9). Allah reinforced him with angels. Abu Zumayl said: Ibn 'Abbas told me: That day, while a Muslim was pursuing a polytheist in front of him, he heard a whip strike above him and a horseman's voice say: Charge, Hayzum! He looked at the polytheist in front of him and saw him fall flat on his back. When he looked at him, he saw that his nose had been struck and his face split as if by a whip, and all of it had turned green. The Ansari came and told the Messenger of Allah. He said: You have spoken truthfully; that was reinforcement from the third heaven. That day they killed seventy and captured seventy. Abu Zumayl said: Ibn 'Abbas said: When they had taken the captives, the Messenger of Allah asked Abu Bakr and 'Umar: What do you think about these captives? Abu Bakr said: Prophet of Allah, they are our cousins and kin. I think you should take ransom from them, which will strengthen us against the disbelievers; perhaps Allah will guide them to Islam. The Messenger of Allah said: What do you think, Ibn al-Khattab? I said: No, by Allah, Messenger of Allah, I do not think as Abu Bakr does. I think you should let us overpower them and strike their necks. Let 'Ali overpower 'Aqil and strike his neck, and let me overpower so-and-so, a relative of 'Umar, and strike his neck. These are the leaders and chiefs of disbelief. The Messenger of Allah favored what Abu Bakr said and did not favor what I said. The next morning I came and found the Messenger of Allah and Abu Bakr sitting and weeping. I said: Messenger of Allah, tell me why you and your companion are weeping. If I find cause to weep, I will weep, and if not, I will pretend to weep because you are weeping. The Messenger of Allah said: I am weeping because of what your companions proposed, taking ransom. Their punishment was shown to me closer than that tree—one near the Messenger of Allah. Allah, Mighty and Exalted, then revealed: It is not for a prophet to have captives until he has thoroughly subdued the land (8:67), through His words: So consume what you have taken as spoils, lawful and good (8:69). Allah thus made the spoils lawful for them.
